verdict.link_basis: 163 directly named city rows with independently reviewed unique 2021 endpoints × three annual observation years (2022, 2023, 2024)
verdict.identity_scope: same published city identity in the official table series; retain year-specific published population observations

checked_rule.criterion: Direct named city row in the same official comparative table, with a previously reviewed exact city-row binding to one selected 2021 settlement observation; admit only the identity relationship for the 2022–2024 annual rows.

population_fields.derived_person_count: published integer × 1000 only; does not add precision
population_fields.reference_date: January 1 of each annual year, per footnote 1
population_fields.rounding: published as thousands; rounding convention unspecified, so no precision interval inferred

footnotes.footnote_1: 2002, 2010 and 2021 refer to census dates; other years are estimates as of January 1 of the corresponding year.
footnotes.footnote_2: Balashikha's 2010 and 2021 values include the 2015 boundary change; corresponding row remains held.
footnotes.footnote_3: Moscow includes its 2012 boundary change; corresponding row remains held.

independent_checks.official_source: Compared frozen extracted rows and raw table lines with official Russian Statistical Yearbook 2024, table 4.9, printed pages 90–92 (PDF pages 91–93).

independent_pdf_extraction.result: All 172 source row annual triplets (516 cells) match the 2022, 2023, 2024 columns parsed from PDF pages 91–93; the January 1 estimate footnote is present.

fixed_sample.method: 12 rows sampled deterministically with Python random seed 20261002, four rows from each PDF page containing the table; this is a source-reading check, not a precision sample.
fixed_sample.result: Rows’ Russian labels, source raw lines, and annual cells matched the PDF. Includes high population values Samara and an intentionally held Balashikha; no discrepancy found.

limitations: This is a scoped rule-family review plus deterministic reuse of the prior reviewed bindings; the 12-row check is not evidence of a national error rate.
Annual values are estimates rounded to thousand persons; the source gives no rounding convention. They must not be represented as exact counts or assigned an assumed error interval.
2021 is a census observation as of October 1; 2022–2024 are January 1 estimates. Identity continuity does not make those measurement dates equivalent.
The table covers only listed cities with population of at least 100,000 and is not a national settlement denominator.
Year-specific boundaries and population scopes remain; no boundary harmonization, coordinate transfer, or spatial identity is approved by this review.
